headline: GOLD $4,046 FIRMS AS DOLLAR FALLS; SILVER $58 — PCE IN-LINE REMOVES RATE-HIKE SCARE, METALS HOLD INTO WEEKEND
snippet: Spot gold traded near $4,046 (+0.50%) and spot silver near $58.24 (+0.84%) ahead of Friday's North American open as May PCE inflation came in broadly in line — 4.1% YoY, 3.4% core — removing the immediate upside surprise needed to sustain the week's selloff and pushing the U.S. dollar lower to near 101.22. September rate-hike probability held near 63% and December near 80%, meaning the recovery is tentative, but the in-line data was sufficient to ease the institutional liquidation pressure that had pushed gold below $4,000 earlier in the week.

headline: NUVAU'S FIRST HOLE IN 40 YEARS HITS 5.28 g/t AU OVER 6.1m AT THUNDERMINE — VMS + GOLD SYSTEM CONFIRMED, MATAGAMI (TSXV:NMC)
snippet: Nuvau Minerals (TSXV:NMC) today reported its first-ever drill hole at the Thundermine target in its 100%-owned Matagami Mining Camp, Quebec — a target untested for nearly four decades — returned 5.28 g/t gold over 6.1 metres, including 7.22 g/t over 3.1 metres, simultaneously confirming VMS-style sulphide alteration and a gold-bearing hydrothermal system in a corridor where 1988 channel samples included 78.16 g/t Au over 1.0m. A second rig is now operating and will advance additional gold and base-metal targets at the Lotto and Daniel zones across the camp.

headline: BOLD VENTURES DRILLS BEST GOLD EVER AT TRAXXIN: 100.7 g/t AU OVER 2.95m — EAST VEIN UNDER-TESTED, NW ONTARIO (TSXV:BOL)
snippet: Bold Ventures Inc. (TSXV:BOL) reported June 25 that hole TX-26-02 at the Traxxin Main Zone — 130km west-northwest of Thunder Bay, Ontario — returned 100.7 g/t gold over 2.95m, including 476 g/t over 0.6m, from a quartz vein with visible gold along the under-tested east side of the zone. CEO Bruce MacLachlan called these the highest-grade results in diamond drilling at Traxxin since the original 2016 discovery, and noted the east-side vein strike is structurally underexplored — framing a clear expansion target for the next phase of work, results from companion hole TX-26-01 still pending.

headline: CATL JIANXIAWO RESTART PUSHED 18 MONTHS — LAND APPROVAL CANCELED, 3% OF GLOBAL LITHIUM SUPPLY STAYS OFFLINE
snippet: Analyst coverage from Benchmark Minerals and Edgen confirms CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi Province — suspended since August 2025 after its operating permit lapsed — now faces an 18-month delay after a government land-use assessment cited in last week's restart speculation was subsequently cancelled. The reversal is market-moving: Jianxiawo accounts for roughly 3% of global hard-rock lithium production, and its extended shutdown through at least late 2027 tightens the 2026–2027 supply-demand balance that Citi and Goldman Sachs had modelled on an assumption of imminent resumption.

headline: LITHIUM'S NEW GROWTH ENGINE: GRID STORAGE HITS 31% OF 2026 DEMAND — DATA CENTRES JOIN EVS AS STRUCTURAL DRIVER
snippet: Albemarle and Liontown told analysts June 24 that grid-scale battery energy storage — driven by renewable grid-stability mandates and surging AI data-centre power demand — is now their fastest-growing end market, with lithium demand from storage rising 55% in 2026 and expected to constitute 31% of total lithium consumption, up from 23% in 2025. The demand shift is helping erode the oversupply overhang that has depressed prices since 2023, with S&P Global modelling a potential 22,000-to-80,000-tonne supply deficit by year-end — a structural floor that lithium bear scenarios did not account for when data-centre power loads were not yet a factor.

headline: EASTPORT MAPS 1.4KM URANIUM CORRIDOR IN BOTSWANA — TWO PARALLEL FENCES UP TO 450 PPM U₃O₈ NEAR LETLHAKANE (TSXV:EVI)
snippet: Eastport Critical Metals (TSXV:EVI, OTCQB:EVIIF) announced June 24 that drilling at the Foley Uranium Project in Botswana's Kalahari Basin has now defined two parallel fences of continuous uranium mineralisation — spaced roughly 400m apart, each exceeding 1.4km strike — located only 350–750m north of Lotus Resources' permitted Letlhakane deposit. Highlight intercepts include 6.0m at 203 ppm U₃O₈ from 76m (RC034) and an internal high-grade interval of 2.0m at 450 ppm U₃O₈ from 54m (RC037), with mineralisation open to the north, south, and east — signalling that the discovery footprint is not yet bounded.

headline: ATHABASCA HITS 100%: F4 URANIUM EXPANDS MURPHY LAKE 60% TO 4,000m — EVERY TARGET RETURNS RADIOACTIVITY (TSXV:FFU)
snippet: F4 Uranium Corp. (TSXV:FFU) and operator UraniumX Discovery (CSE:STMN) announced June 23 a 60% expansion of the Murphy Lake drill program in northeastern Athabasca Basin — from 2,500m to 4,000m — after anomalous radioactivity was detected in 100% of all target areas drilled to date; discovery hole ML26-021 intersected strong limonite, bleaching, and clay alteration in sandstone above the unconformity plus radioactivity in basement rocks immediately below the contact, the archetypal signature of a world-class Athabasca unconformity deposit. The fully UraniumX-funded property sits 30km northwest of Orano's McLean Lake deposits and adjacent to ISOEnergy's Hurricane Uranium Deposit.

headline: NIOBAY'S CREVIER NIOBIUM SUMMER DRILL BEGINS — FIRST CAMPAIGN AFTER INAUGURAL MEASURED RESOURCE; GIRARDVILLE, QUEBEC (TSXV:NBY)
snippet: NioBay Metals (TSXV:NBY) announced June 23 the commencement of its 2026 drill campaign at the Crevier Niobium and Tantalum Project in Quebec — a 72.5%-owned asset located roughly 50km north of Girardville — marking the first drilling since an updated February 2026 resource estimate that included the property's inaugural Measured classification. Niobium is a NATO-listed critical mineral used primarily in high-strength steel alloys and aerospace components, with more than 90% of global primary supply currently concentrated in Brazil — a strategic geography that has attracted increasing attention from Western industrial buyers seeking supply chain alternatives.

headline: GERMANIUM $2,673/KG CHINA, $6,150/KG WESTERN — 130% EXPORT-CONTROL PREMIUM WIDENS AS JUNE EXTENDS RECORD 2026 RUN
snippet: Germanium reached $2,673.66/kg in China's domestic market in June 2026 — up approximately 30% from April's $2,049/kg — while Western in-warehouse buyers paid approximately $6,150/kg as of June 1, a 130% premium reflecting the direct impact of China's August 2023 export licensing controls on semiconductor-grade material. Unlike terbium (covered in last session), germanium is a metalloid whose primary Western demand channels — defence infrared optics, fibre-optic cable manufacturing, and solar panel production — are all simultaneously scaling, meaning the licensing squeeze is hitting a structurally growing demand base rather than a static one.

headline: SILVER 47% BELOW JANUARY PEAK, SIXTH SUPPLY DEFICIT YEAR INTACT — GOLDSILVER.COM: "THE CORRECTION WAS THE SETUP"
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 silver outlook argues the metal's 47% collapse from January's all-time high is creating a historically attractive re-entry into a structurally deficit commodity: supply deficits are now running for a sixth consecutive year, China continues importing silver at record pace for solar and EV manufacturing, and physical demand fundamentals are entirely unchanged — what changed is institutional positioning driven by real-rate sensitivity, not the supply-demand balance. The thesis: rate-driven corrections in structurally deficit assets don't resolve the deficit — they compress the entry window for investors who understand the difference.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: CHINA IMPORTS 790+ TONNES SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — THREE MAJOR EXCHANGES DRAINING SIMULTANEOUSLY
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis flags silver physical demand as the standout positive in a week dominated by institutional selling: China imported more than 790 tonnes of silver in the early months of 2026 — a record pace tied to domestic solar manufacturing capacity additions — while the Shanghai Futures Exchange, COMEX, and LBMA warehouses are all declining simultaneously, a three-exchange inventory drawdown not seen in over a decade. Nearly one billion ounces of silver have exited visible global inventory since 2021, building a structural floor that rate-cycle narratives obscure but cannot erase.
